title: 建築のための数理工Ⅱ
subtitle: Integrated Math and Science for Architecture II
courseType:
Mathematics and Science Program
Mathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) differentiation (2) integration (3) first moment of area
advice: This is a basic course in calculus for students in the Dept. of Architecture. We will cover the following topics: 1. Differentiation 2. Integration 3. Integration issues (basic applications of differentiation and integration to various problems in architecture) Extra classes may be held depending the comprehension level of students. Students are required to review and preview each class. As a matter of particular emphasis, students are required to attempt the exercises following each class. Extra materials may be distributed if necessary. In their assignments, students are required to show their solution/calculation procedure logically and clearly. Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or office hours of the teacher.
books: Textbooks:Integrated Math and Science for Architecture I II [Kanazawa Institute of Technology] Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: Basic calculation skills for numerical formulas (expansion, factorization, division, and calculation of fractional formulas).

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of differentiation and find derivatives of basic functions.
Be able to find indefinite integrals of basic functions and calculate the value of basic definite integrals.
Be able to explain various problems in architecture using differentiation and integration.
Be able to demonstrate an understanding of all topics, attend every class, and do the required work.
Understand the meanings of fundamental English words for mathematics.
